To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we isolated a novel cDNA from the chick growth plate that is more highly transcribed in the proliferating chondrocyte than in the hypertrophic chondrocye and we mapped the gene to chromosome 1, the chromosome carrying the autosomal dwarfism gene.
we have identified a gene expressed differentially in proliferating and hypertrophic chondrogenic cells and mapped it to chromosome 1 of the chicken.

we have cloned a novel cDNA, named CPGP (chondrocyte proliferation gene product) that encodes a 308 amino acid integral membrane protein, that this cDNA is more highly expressed by proliferating chondrocyte cells in the growth plate, that the CPGP gene is located on chicken chromosome 1 close to a dwarfism locus, and that the CPGp gene is expressed in a wide variety of tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel gene which may play a role in the regulation of chondrocyte proliferation.
the isolation and characterisation of a novel gene, which is differentially expressed between proliferating and hypertrophic chondocytes of the growth plate.
the identification of genes expressed in the chick tibiotarsal growth plate and the mapping of these genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein product of the gene identified is an integral membrane protein which is expressed differentially in the proliferating chondrocyte zone of the chick growth cartilage.
the novel cDNA clone described in this paper encodes a putative trans-membrane protein that may have a role in the regulation of growth in the chick growth cartilage.

the protein is a novel integral membrane protein, which is expressed in all tissues, and that it is more highly expressed at the mRNA level in proliferative rather than hypertrophic growth plate chondrocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the novel integral membrane protein described here is differentially expressed between the proliferative and hypertrophic regions of the chick growth plates.

the gene described in this paper is a novel integral membrane protein that is expressed at a higher level in proliferating rather that hypertrophic chondocytes of the chick growthplate and that it is located on the short arm of chromosome 1 close to the locus of dwarfism.
we have cloned a novel integral membrane protein that is expressed differentially in the growth plate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to identify a novel protein that is expressed in the growth plate and may have a role in regulating growth.
the gene is differentially expressed and that it maps close to the dwarfism locus.
the gene is expressed in a tissue-specific manner and may play a role in chondrocyte proliferation and/or maturation.
